mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days without requiring specific threshold conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS has declined over the prior 3 months, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 2.0%, it signals a tightening monetary policy that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 2.0%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in the federal funds rate and unemployment rate signal a monetary tightening cycle coinciding with labor market weakness, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced economic growth prospects.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE have increased by at least 0.2 percentage points over the prior 3 months, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of low unemployment (UNRATE < 4.0%), the labor market is tight, supporting strong consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE < 4.0%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) indicate strong consumer demand for residential construction, which correlates with broader economic expansion and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days without requiring specific threshold conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where HOUST has increased by at least 1.0% over the prior month, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100, it signals a contraction in manufacturing output, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced economic activity.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where INDPRO < 100, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) indicate a broad-based economic slowdown across both the housing sector and manufacturing, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where both HOUST and INDPRO have declined by at least 1.0% over the prior month, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of high consumer spending (RSAFS > 500000) and low inflation (CPIAUCSL < 2.5%), strong demand for goods and services supports corporate revenue growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: high consumer spending with low inflation
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where RSAFS > 500000 and CPIAUCSL < 2.5%, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.
